title: Centered second coordinate moment
statement:
Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $c=(c_j)_{j\in I}\in\mathbb R^I$, let $v\ge0$, and choose $i\in I$. If $Z=(Z_j)_{j\in I}$ has independent Gaussian coordinates with means $c_j$ and common variance $v$, then
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^I}(z_i-c_i)^2\,d\Bigl(\bigotimes_{j\in I}N(c_j,v)\Bigr)(z)=v.
\]
replaced: For a finite set $I$, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v\ge0$, and $i\in I$, $\int(z_i-c_i)^2\,d(\bigotimes_jN(c_j,v))(z)=v$.
